;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[June 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]; [[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**Two [[Afghanistan Independent Human Rights Commission]] workers are killed when a [[improvised explosive device|bomb]] attached to their vehicle explodes in [[Kabul]]. The [[Taliban]] denies responsibility and no other group has claimed responsibility. The attack is condemned by the [[United Nations]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attacks-rights/two-afghan-human-rights-workers-killed-in-blast-in-kabul-idUSKBN23Y0H9?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**An [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]]-affiliated group attacks a town near billion-dollar gas projects managed by [[Total S.A.]] and [[Exxon Mobil]] in [[Mocímboa da Praia]], [[Mozambique]]. An army spokesman reports that the [[Mozambique Defence Armed Forces|armed forces]] suffered casualties in the attack. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mozambique-insurgency/insurgents-stage-very-violent-attack-close-to-gas-projects-in-mozambique-idUSKBN23Y0OU?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Hinduism in Pakistan]]
**The government of Prime Minister [[Imran Khan]] approves a grant of [[Pakistani rupee|Rs]]100 million for the construction of the [[Shri Krishna Mandir, Islamabad|first Hindu temple]] in the capital of [[Islamabad]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1565405/pm-approves-grant-for-construction-of-hindu-temple-in-islamabad (DAWN)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
**[[India]] surpasses 500,000 cases after reporting 18,552 new cases in the last 24 hours, the highest toll to date. India also reports a total 15,685 deaths from the disease. [https://apnews.com/114bde59882c280e6e68682e0418af11 (AP News)]

;International relations
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Libyan Civil War]], [[Wagner Group]]
**[[Libya]]'s international-recognized government, the [[Government of National Accord]], calls for the [[United States]] and the [[European Union]] to impose sanctions on individuals and "[[mercenaries]]", after its [[National Oil Corporation]] stated that [[Russia]]n mercenaries and other foreign actors had forced their way into the [[Sharara oilfield]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/libya-calls-eu-sanctions-russian-mercenaries-backers-200627112137004.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[Red Bluff shooting]]
**An employee is killed and four others injured in a [[mass shooting]] at a [[Walmart]] distribution center in [[Red Bluff, California]], [[United States]]. The shooter was then confronted by responding police officers and fatally shot during a [[shootout]]. [https://apnews.com/a5ebbf3806e1abaa6cee11af80c415da (AP News)]
*[[Breonna Taylor protests]]
**One person is killed and another injured when a gunman opened fire at people protesting the [[Killing of Breonna Taylor|killing]] of [[Breonna Taylor]] in [[Louisville, Kentucky|Louisville]], [[Kentucky]], United States. [https://apnews.com/b31cb9fa8c18f9ec8d7ac66e13566543 (AP News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Hong Kong 1 July marches]]
**[[Hong Kong Police Force|Police]] in [[Hong Kong]] ban the 1 July march for the first time in 17 years. In a letter of objection addressed to protest organizer and convenor of the [[Civil Human Rights Front]] (CHRF) [[Jimmy Sham]], police cite "persisting social unrest" and [[vandalism]]. Chief Secretary [[Matthew Cheung]] rejects an appeal by the CHRF who have said they will appeal the ban. [https://hongkongfp.com/2020/06/27/breaking-hong-kong-police-ban-annual-pro-democracy-demo-for-first-time-in-17-years/ (Hong Kong Free Press)]
*[[2020 Icelandic presidential election]]
**Citizens of [[Iceland]] cast their vote in the latest [[Elections in Iceland|presidential elections]]. Incumbent [[President of Iceland|president]] [[Guðni Th. Jóhannesson]] is expected to be the clear winner of the election. [https://www.dw.com/en/icelands-incumbent-president-set-for-landslide-election-win/a-53963966 (DW)]
*[[2020 Irish general election#Government formation|Irish government formation]]
**Following long negotiations, the [[Government of the 33rd Dáil|new Irish government]] is voted into office by [[Dáil Éireann]]. The [[government of Ireland|government]] is formed after a historic coalition deal between [[Fianna Fáil]], [[Fine Gael]] and the [[Green Party (Ireland)|Green Party]]. Fianna Fáil leader [[Micheál Martin]] takes office as [[Taoiseach]] (Prime Minister), with outgoing Taoiseach [[Leo Varadkar]] as [[Tánaiste]] (Deputy Prime Minister), due to return to the post in December 2022 as part of the coalition deal. [https://www.rte.ie/news/politics/2020/0625/1149711-programme-for-government/ (RTÉ)]
*[[2020 Malawian presidential election]]
**[[Lazarus Chakwera]] has been elected [[President of Malawi|President]] with 58.57% of the votes. [https://www.nyasatimes.com/chakwera-declared-winner-of-malawi-presidential-election-defeats-incumbent-mutharika/ (''Nyasa Times'')]
